Hi Sam — Vivek here from Redwood InfoSec. Attached is a draft subprocessor dependency matrix that answers the fields you listed: vendor, service/purpose, data types (tokens, request metadata, logs, user-provided content), data residency, contractual assurance, and link to evidence where available.

Quick summary of major subprocessors (high level):
- AWS (us-west-2): primary compute and object storage (S3). SOC 2 referenced in evidence pack.
- GCP (us-east1): batch inference/analytics for some customers; SOC 2 referenced.
- Datadog: monitoring/metrics; processes aggregated telemetry and host metrics. SOC 2 attestation available from Datadog.
- Sentry: error tracking (limited telemetry); we scrub PII before sending.
- Segment / RudderStack: event routing for product analytics (only with customer opt-in).
- Intercom / Zendesk: customer support communications (instances segregated by tenant; access controlled).
- PagerDuty: on-call alerts (only metadata and alert text; no raw customer content).
- Cloudflare: CDN and WAF for edge protections.
- Postgres (managed): customer data stored in primary DB; hosted on AWS RDS.

Notes on telemetry and PII: we do not forward raw customer PII to error-tracking services. We mask or truncate tokens and any fields flagged as sensitive by our parsers before shipping. Where customers elect to send full logs (rare), we document that separately and require contractual approval.

Attachments and links included:
- subprocessor_dependency_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- subprocessor_evidence_pack.zip (includes SOC 2 excerpts and vendor attestation links)
- SOC2-Redwood-2025.pdf (our SOC 2 report redacted)
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-SubprocessorEvidence

If you'd like, we can produce a dataset-specific mapping for any hosts you plan to send. Also happy to set a short call with our vendor contacts (e.g., Jenna Park at CloudInfra) if you need direct confirmation.

-Vivek

Hi Sam — quick answers inline and next steps.

On Mon, Apr 12, 2026 at 4:30 PM Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> 1) Telemetry retention: can you confirm default retention periods for aggregated telemetry (Datadog) and error events (Sentry)?

- Datadog: metrics retained by default for 15 months (with rollup/aggregation after 90 days). Detailed logs (if enabled) retained 7 days by default unless otherwise configured.
- Sentry: error events retained 30 days by default; we configure scrubbing and retention per-customer when needed.

> 2) PII controls: appreciate the masking note. Can you point to the exact fields your scrubbing pipeline removes by default (or share the scrubbing rules)?

- By default our scrubbing pipeline removes: any fields named or matching regexes for email, phone, SSN, credit_card, and fields flagged by our semantic-sensitive detector (e.g., personal name tokens adjacent to numeric sequences). We also truncate long text blobs and remove bearer tokens/authorization headers. We can provide the scrubbing rule list as a short export (attached).

> 3) For CloudInfra ... can you share a primary contact?

- Primary contact: Jenna Park (jenna.park@cloudinfra.io). I've included her on the original request thread so your team can reach out.

> 4) DPA signature?

- Yes — here's a DocuSign link for the standard Redwood DPA: https://app.docusign.com/recipient/embedded?envelopeId=0a1b2c (or we can route via your procurement).

Attachments: telemetry_data_flow_diagram.png (diagram showing mask->scrub->route stages), and I've asked our legal team to prepare a redline-friendly DPA if you prefer.

If helpful, we can run a 20-min call later this week to walk through specific SIG questions; Laura will coordinate scheduling.

Thanks,
